tone.quote: Trans-New Guinea Phylum / Sepik-Ramu Phylum / Torricelli Phylum -- PHONOLOGY ... Vowel phonemes with wide range of allophones : no / yes / yes ; vowel sequences : present / absent / present ; Phonologically relevant tones : often present / rare / absent ; Morphonemic changes : common / few / few
tone.locator: p. 265, table in sec. 6.4 'Comparison of features' (Torricelli Phylum column); table introduced p. 264 as based on Wurm, Laycock and Voorhoeve (1975:179-186)
tone.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)
tone.says: Phylum-level typological table only (sec. 6.4, p. 265, compiled from Wurm, Laycock & Voorhoeve 1975:179-186): 'Phonologically relevant tones' = often present (Trans-New Guinea) / rare (Sepik-Ramu) / absent (Torricelli Phylum). The described language is Au [avt]; Bragat appears only as language no. 22 in the Torricelli family tree (p. 263). No Bragat-specific tone, stress or pitch data; 'tone absent' applies to Bragat only by inheritance from the phylum generalisation and must not be filed as a…

sources.citation: Laycock, Donald C. 1975. The Torricelli Phylum. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study 1, 767-780. Pacific Linguistics C-38.
sources.note: Phylum-level segmental summary only (p.769: three positions of articulation, usually no voicing contrast, 5-8 vowels, many fricatives); nothing on stress; Bragat appears only in the checklist.

sources.citation: Laycock, Donald C. 1968. Languages of the Lumi Subdistrict (West Sepik District), New Guinea. Oceanic Linguistics 7(1): 36-66.
sources.note: The only primary publication with any Bragat data ('a few words', Laycock 1973); also has family-level typological notes for the Palei group that could contain a remark on stress. Low expectation but it is the sole primary item.

sources.citation: The Rosetta Project. n.d. Bragat Swadesh List (10 glosses, each in two transcriptions, evidently extracted from Laycock 1968 Table 2). Internet Archive item rosettaproject_aof_swadesh-1.
sources.note: No prose at all. Acute accents on 8 of 10 items (7 on the first syllable, 1 on the second: yëmáing 'breast'); these are wordlist stress MARKS only, not a statement, and their convention (Laycock's or Barnes's) is unverified.
